headline_en: Body of Dipali, Bangladeshi woman worker killed in Israeli strike in Lebanon, to arrive home Thursday
summary_en: The body of Dipali Begum (34), a Bangladeshi woman worker from Faridpur who was fatally injured in an Israeli air strike on a building in Beirut on 8 April 2026, is to reach Dhaka airport about a month later, on Thursday 7 May 2026 via Dubai. The embassy in Beirut completed the police report and body-transport permit. The Faridpur Probashi Kalyan Centre says the body will be sent home by free government ambulance and the family will get BDT 35,000 for burial at the airport and BDT 300,000 later.

facts.statement: Dipali Begum (34), a Bangladeshi woman worker in Lebanon (also printed as Dipali Akter), was seriously injured in an Israeli air strike on a building in Beirut on 8 April 2026 and later died under treatment at Rafik Hariri Hospital in Beirut.

Dipali Begum's body was to leave Beirut airport on an Emirates flight on Wednesday (about 6 May 2026) at 3:45 pm local time and, via Dubai, land on another flight at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, on Thursday (about 7 May 2026) at 11:20 pm Bangladesh time, about one month after her death.
facts.source_in_article: message signed by Mohammad Anwar Hossain, First Secretary (Labour) and head of mission, Bangladesh Embassy, Beirut

facts.statement: For repatriating the body of a Bangladeshi worker killed in Lebanon, the Bangladesh Embassy in Beirut said it had completed all administrative steps, including obtaining a certified police report and a permit to send the body; meanwhile the body was kept in the morgue of Rafik Hariri Hospital, Beirut.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh Embassy, Beirut (message signed by First Secretary (Labour) Mohammad Anwar Hossain)

facts.statement: The family of a worker killed in Lebanon was contacted by the Bangladesh Embassy in Beirut and by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to confirm the arrival of the body; the sister expected to receive the body after airport formalities, possibly by 2 am the same night.
facts.source_in_article: Laizu Begum, younger sister of the deceased

facts.statement: The body of a Bangladeshi worker killed in Lebanon took about a month to bring home because of the war situation and because air traffic was not normal.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Ashik Siddiqui, Assistant Director, Faridpur Probashi Kalyan Centre

facts.statement: After the body of the worker killed in Lebanon arrives in Bangladesh, it will be sent to the village home in a free ambulance under government arrangement; family members will be handed BDT 35,000 at the airport for burial costs and later given BDT 300,000 (three lakh taka) in financial assistance.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Ashik Siddiqui, Assistant Director, Faridpur Probashi Kalyan Centre

facts.statement: Dipali, daughter of day labourer Sheikh Moka of Purbo Shalepur Munshirchar village, Charbhadrasan upazila, Faridpur, went to Lebanon in 2011 at the age of 19 to relieve family poverty and supported her family with her earnings abroad.

The Faridpur District Probashi Kalyan Centre (Assistant Director Md. Ashik Siddiqui) and the Bangladesh Embassy in Beirut were the sources confirming body repatriation arrangements for a worker from Faridpur killed in Lebanon.

headline_en: 'Cox's Bazar has become a human trafficking route'
summary_en: At a day-long BRAC Migration Programme workshop for journalists in Cox's Bazar on 20 April 2026, speakers said Cox's Bazar has become a sea route for human trafficking, that trafficking across the Andaman Sea has increased recently and that many are dying. facts.source_in_article: speakers at BRAC Migration Programme workshop, Cox's Bazar

facts.statement: BRAC associate director Shariful Hasan said that would-be migrants going to Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries are falling into the hands of brokers and putting their lives at risk.

Cox's Bazar journalists at the workshop said human trafficking through the Cox's Bazar coast can be controlled if preparations are made and the public is made aware.

headline_en: 'I never had to pour my own glass of water; what am I doing abroad now'
summary_en: Profile of Fahim Ahmad Munna (20), an HSC candidate from Doarabazar, Sunamganj, who left home on 16 February 2026, went to Saudi Arabia for two days, was taken to Libya and put on a rubber boat ('game') to Greece on 21 March. The boat lost its way for six days and he died from lack of food and drinking water; the bodies were thrown into the sea. He was sent through a relative acting as broker.

facts.statement: Fahim Ahmad Munna (20) of Kabirnagar village, Doarabazar, Sunamganj left home on 16 February 2026, went to Saudi Arabia where he stayed two days, was then taken to Libya, and on 21 March 2026 was put with others on a 'game' (small rubber boat) from Libya towards Greece.

facts.statement: According to a youth from the same area who was on the boat, the boat from Libya to Greece carried 38 people, lost its way and stayed at sea six days; 18 people including Fahim died from lack of food and clean water, their bodies stayed on the boat for two days and were then thrown into the sea. facts.statement: The boat reached the coast of Greece on 27 March 2026; the survivors were rescued and taken to a camp there.

Boglabazar Union Parishad chairman Mohammad Milon Khan said many people from the area are going to Europe illegally, lured by human trafficking rings with the hope of a better life, that this is extremely risky, and that everyone should be aware.

headline_en: 12 of those who died in the Mediterranean are from Sunamganj; bodies were thrown into the sea

Survivors are held in a camp in Greece. headline_en: 22 migrants die off Greek coast; 21 Bangladeshis rescued alive
summary_en: At least 22 migrants died after drifting six days without food or water on a rubber boat that left Tobruk, eastern Libya, on 21 March 2026 for Greece. A European border agency vessel rescued 26 people off Crete, including 21 Bangladeshis, 4 South Sudanese and one Chadian. Bodies were thrown into the sea on a smuggler's order; Greek authorities arrested two South Sudanese suspected smugglers.

facts.statement: At least 22 migrants died off the coast of Greece after drifting for six days at sea on a rubber boat travelling from North Africa to Europe, according to survivors' statements to the Greek coast guard on Saturday 28 March 2026.

On Friday 27 March 2026 the Greek coast guard said a European border agency vessel rescued 26 people alive, including a woman and a child, off the island of Crete; the survivors were 21 Bangladeshis, 4 South Sudanese and one citizen of Chad.

The boat set out for Greece on 21 March 2026 from Tobruk, a port city in eastern Libya; passengers lost direction and drifted six days without food and water. When found it was 53 nautical miles (about 91 km) south of Ierapetra, a town on the south coast of Crete.

headline_en: 12% of HIV cases detected in Bangladesh are migrant workers; sent home as soon as infected
summary_en: A feature on Bangladeshi migrant workers and HIV: in the 2025 reporting year 1,891 people were found HIV-infected in Bangladesh, 12% of them returnees from abroad. Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE and other Middle Eastern countries do not allow HIV-positive foreigners to stay; detection at a work-permit renewal medical or a hospital visit leads to visa cancellation and quick deportation without treatment or counselling. Experts criticise the practice and Bangladesh's weak pre-departure health education, embassy support and reintegration services.

facts.statement: According to the National AIDS and STD Control Programme of the Directorate General of Health Services, 1,891 people were found infected with HIV in Bangladesh in 2025 (December 2024 to November 2025); 12% of them were people who had returned from abroad.

In Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other Middle Eastern countries, foreigners infected with HIV are not permitted to stay under immigration and public health laws (the countries' Immigration Act, Public Health Law or Residence Regulation).

In Middle Eastern countries (Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE and others), HIV is usually detected in the mandatory medical test at work permit renewal or when a worker goes to hospital ill; if detected, the visa is cancelled and the worker is quickly sent back to the home country.

A young construction company worker from a north-eastern district of Bangladesh, after one year in a Middle Eastern country, tested HIV positive in a routine hospital test; the hospital informed that country's health ministry, which informed immigration; within days his visa was cancelled and work permission ended, and he was sent home quickly with no treatment plan, counselling or discussion of next steps.
facts.source_in_article: reporter; Mir, president of Brave Dimension Global

facts.statement: An HIV-negative certificate is mandatory before going abroad for work from Bangladesh, but there is no effective training on risk reduction or sexual health; pre-departure briefing covers HIV, safe behaviour and the right to health care abroad only in a very limited way.

The Bangladesh government supplies antiretroviral (ARV) medicine free of charge, but counselling, mental health support and livelihood rehabilitation for HIV-positive returnees are very limited; the returned worker in the article received counselling from a non-government organisation, not from any government body.
facts.source_in_article: reporter; Mir, president of Brave Dimension Global

facts.statement: Bangladeshi missions abroad are not playing a major role on HIV; in most cases infected workers do not get legal or medical help from the embassy.
According to Tasneem Siddiqui of RMMRU, Middle Eastern countries also immediately send back any woman worker who becomes pregnant, not only HIV-positive workers.
facts.source_in_article: Tasneem Siddiqui, acting executive director, RMMRU

facts.statement: In some destination countries workers fear losing their job if they take an HIV test, so workers avoid testing despite risk; sexual and reproductive health care is not easily available to migrant workers in many destination countries. Risk factors named: long separation from family, loneliness, mental stress and limited knowledge of safe sexual behaviour.

The ILO and WHO have clearly said that expelling someone solely for HIV infection is discriminatory and a human rights violation; the article says removing job and residence rights on health grounds is contrary to the ICCPR and the Migrant Workers Convention.

Tasneem Siddiqui (RMMRU) said health care should be mentioned when bilateral agreements or MoUs on migration are signed, though it is unlikely to be effective, and Bangladesh should raise these demands in international multilateral forums; she called the immediate-deportation rule inhumane and said the receiving country is responsible for a sick migrant worker's treatment.
facts.source_in_article: Tasneem Siddiqui, acting executive director, RMMRU

facts.statement: Experts recommend: mandatory, practical pre-departure health education especially on HIV and sexual health; strongly raising an end to HIV-based deportation in bilateral talks with destination countries; and a separate structure for rehabilitation, employment and mental health support for infected returnee workers.

BRAC associate director Shariful Hasan said Bangladesh has more than one crore (10 million) migrant workers, most working in Saudi Arabia, UAE and other Middle Eastern countries, and that HIV infection among Bangladeshi migrants is comparatively low; he said returnees who are infected should be assured treatment and counselling after return and migrant workers should be aware and responsible.

headline_en: Saudi Arabia top source of remittances, followed by UK and UAE
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank data for July-November of FY2025-26 show Saudi Arabia again the top remittance source (USD 2.05 billion), followed by the UK, UAE, Malaysia and the US. Bankers say the US had topped the list after August 2024 because US-owned remittance companies were recorded as US-origin even when money was sent from other countries, which has now been corrected. Total remittances for 1 July-30 November 2025 were USD 13.03 billion.

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank data: in July-November 2025 remittances by source country were Saudi Arabia USD 205 crore (highest), United Kingdom USD 167 crore, UAE USD 158 crore, Malaysia USD 143 crore, United States USD 103 crore, Italy USD 83 crore, Oman USD 77 crore, Kuwait USD 64 crore, Qatar USD 59 crore and Singapore USD 55 crore.

After the political change of August 2024 the United States had become the top recorded source of remittances; it has now dropped to fifth. Bank officials said some remittance companies are US-owned and money sent through them from other countries was shown as originating in the US; after this was corrected the country-wise picture is accurate.

Total remittances to Bangladesh from 1 July to 30 November of FY2025-26 were USD 1,303 crore. In November 2025 six state-owned banks brought USD 58.70 crore, Krishi Bank USD 29.59 crore, private banks USD 199.68 crore and foreign banks USD 59 lakh.
Remittances were USD 3,033 crore in FY2024-25 and USD 2,391 crore in FY2023-24; March 2025 saw a record USD 329 crore, the highest for any single month so far.
In the first 17 days of December 2025 expatriates sent more than USD 2 billion (200 crore); bankers expected the month to exceed USD 3 billion if the trend continued.
Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange reserve stood at USD 32.57 billion (3,257 crore) on the Thursday before 20 December 2025; the article says the dollar crisis is over.

The article states that the most Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia; many workers have also gone to UAE, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and Malaysia, while students and skilled professionals have gone to the US and UK.

headline_en: 'I paid the broker 21 lakh taka to send my son to Italy, and still he became a corpse'
summary_en: Two men from Muksudpur, Gopalganj - Anis Sheikh (25) and Enamul Sheikh (28) - died when boats sank off Al-Khums, Libya, on the night of 13 November 2025 on the way to Italy; six more from Muksudpur are missing. Enamul's father says the coast guard chased the boat and it sank while fleeing, and that he had paid a Madaripur broker BDT 21 lakh. The family is appealing for the body to be brought home.

facts.statement: On the night of 13 November 2025 two boats sank off the Al-Khums coast of Libya on the Mediterranean; two men from Muksudpur upazila, Gopalganj died: Anis Sheikh (25), son of Zahid Sheikh, and Enamul Sheikh (28), son of Akbar Ali Sheikh, both of Paschim Loukhanda village, Nanikhir union. Families learned of the deaths via Facebook.

Six more young men from Muksudpur upazila are reported missing in the same Libya boat sinking: Ibrahim Sheikh (son of Awlad Sheikh), Abul Sheikh (son of Haider Sheikh), Dulal Mina (son of Ekram Mina), Ashik Mina (son of Haider Mina) and Sohel Molla (son of Khalek Molla), all of Kashalia village, and Niaz Mina (son of Hafiz Mina) of Gunhar village.

The families of the two dead said one of the sunken boats carried 26 Bangladeshi citizens and four bodies were recovered after the incident; they confirmed Enamul's and Anis's deaths after gathering information over the following days.

Enamul Sheikh left Bangladesh on 10 October 2025 and boarded a boat from the Al-Khums coast of Libya on the night of 13 November 2025; after a short distance the coast guard chased the boat and it sank while trying to flee.

facts.source_in_article: Akbar Ali, father of Enamul Sheikh

headline_en: Attempt to traffic two young men visiting Cox's Bazar to Thailand by sea
summary_en: RAB and BGB rescued 84 people on 21 September 2025 from a traffickers' den in the deep hills of Kachchhapia, Baharchhara, Teknaf, where they had been gathered to be trafficked by sea to Malaysia and Thailand; 66 were Rohingya camp residents. Two Munshiganj youths had been invited to Cox's Bazar by an acquaintance, handed to traffickers and held for 20 days. Three men were arrested with weapons.

facts.statement: On Sunday 21 September 2025 a joint RAB-BGB operation of about 12 hours rescued 84 people, including women and children, from a traffickers' den in the deep hills of Kachchhapia, Baharchhara, Teknaf, where they had been gathered for trafficking by sea to Malaysia and Thailand; 66 of the 84 were residents of Rohingya camps.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Ashikur Rahman, commander, Teknaf-2 BGB, and Lt Col Kamrul Hasan, commander, RAB-15

facts.statement: Amit Hasan and Manik Mia of Munshiganj Sadar met Md. Nur, a Cox's Bazar resident who had stayed in their area for a while; at his invitation they came to Cox's Bazar on 2 September 2025 and went to his house in Moricha, Ukhiya; saying he would take them sightseeing in Teknaf, he put them in an autorickshaw and handed them to human traffickers, who held them in a hill den for 20 days to send them to Thailand by sea.
facts.source_in_article: Amit Hasan and Manik Mia, victims

facts.statement: The two Munshiganj youths said the traffickers beat them whenever they asked to speak to their families by mobile phone while they were held in the hill den.
facts.source_in_article: Amit Hasan and Manik Mia, victims

facts.statement: Apart from the two taken by force, the others rescued from the Teknaf den had been brought with various lures: many were promised a better life and jobs in Malaysia or Thailand, and several women were lured with promises of marriage.

A rescued young woman from a Rohingya camp said she was married by mobile phone on 15 September 2025 to a Rohingya man living in Malaysia; the 'husband' told her to meet some people to go to Malaysia by sea; on 19 September she left the camp, met them and was taken to the hill den. No money was demanded from her; her husband was to pay some money after she reached Malaysia.
facts.source_in_article: a rescued young woman, speaking at Teknaf-2 BGB headquarters

facts.statement: Three men were arrested with arms in the Teknaf operation: Abdullah (21), son of Salamat Ullah of Kachchhapia, Baharchhara union; Saiful Islam (20), son of Abul Hossain of Rajarchhara; and Md. Ibrahim (20), son of Md. Firoz of the same area. Seized: a one-shooter gun, a single-barrel gun, a foreign pistol, two local ramdas, a knife and three live rounds. A case was filed at Teknaf police station.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Ashikur Rahman, Teknaf-2 BGB

facts.statement: During the raid traffickers fired three shots at the joint forces and tried to escape using some victims as shields; the forces surrounded the whole hill and rescued the victims unharmed.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Ashikur Rahman, Teknaf-2 BGB

facts.statement: According to law-enforcement sources, 65 human traffickers were arrested and 161 people rescued in Teknaf in 2025 up to about 22 September; trafficking incidents happen more in the winter season.

headline_en: Singapore bank's decision puts three Bangladeshi banks in trouble
summary_en: Singapore's DBS Bank told remittance houses in early August 2025 that it would no longer accept remittance cash, threatening the legal channel used by Agrani, National and Prime Bank's Singapore remittance operations; about half of Bangladeshi workers' remittances from Singapore are deposited in cash. After Bangladesh Bank intervened, DBS agreed to keep accepting cash until 31 October 2025. The article gives remittance and BMET worker-outflow figures for Singapore.

facts.statement: In early August 2025 DBS Bank told several remittance houses in Singapore that it would no longer accept any remittance cash; at Bangladesh Bank's request DBS agreed to continue accepting cash until 31 October 2025. Preventing money laundering is cited as the reason.

About half of the remittances sent by Bangladeshis working in Singapore are deposited in cash: the money goes first to remittance houses, which deposit it with DBS Bank, and from there it comes to Bangladesh. If cash acceptance stops, remittance houses could take the money but not send it home, and hundi (illegal transfer) could rise.

Bangladesh's Agrani, National and Prime banks have provided remittance services in Singapore since 2006. Agrani Bank has five branches and the other two banks three each in Singapore; these take remittances and also offer deposits and other services, and a large share of Bangladeshi workers there rely on them to send money home.

The three Bangladeshi banks once had accounts with Standard Chartered, UOB and OCBC banks in Singapore, but those relationships were cut about four years ago over money-laundering allegations, heavy use of cash and non-compliance; now they have a transaction relationship only with DBS Bank.
Islami Bank also brings remittances from Singapore through Mustafa Foreign Exchange; NBL Money Transfer operates in Singapore (CEO Shahidul Islam Azad).

Shahidul Islam Azad, CEO of NBL Money Transfer in Singapore, said a sudden stop to cash acceptance would create a major crisis, the income could go through illegal channels, and expatriates need time to get used to digital transactions.
facts.source_in_article: Shahidul Islam Azad, CEO, NBL Money Transfer, Singapore

facts.statement: Former ABB chairman Anis A Khan said Bangladeshis in Singapore earn with great hardship, their pay is quite low and many are paid wages in cash, so ending cash remittance transactions would cause them big problems and risk a rise in illegal hundi.
facts.source_in_article: Anis A Khan, former chairman, Association of Bankers Bangladesh

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank data: remittances from Singapore were USD 38.52 crore in FY2021-22 and USD 42.33 crore in FY2022-23. In FY2024-25 monthly figures were: July USD 4.27 crore, August 2.69 crore, September 2.46 crore, October 4.22 crore, November 4.47 crore, December 6.04 crore, January 7.16 crore, February 7.30 crore, March 4.74 crore and April 5.09 crore.

BMET data: 64,383 people went from Bangladesh to work in Singapore in 2022, 53,265 in 2023 and 58,878 in 2024; 26,389 went from January to May 2025; from 2004 to May 2025 a total of 919,159 went to Singapore.

Singapore has for several years been one of the top five destinations for Bangladeshi migrant workers; most workers there are hired in construction and shipbuilding, and the country takes only skilled workers.

headline_en: Bangladeshi worker crushed to death under a crane in Malaysia
summary_en: Farhad Hossain alias Rony (31) of Sharsha, Jashore died on Saturday 5 July 2025 in Seremban, Malaysia when a crane chain snapped at a building site and he was crushed. He had gone in January 2023 at a cost of BDT 5 lakh, borrowed by his father and not yet fully repaid. Fellow Bangladeshi workers were trying to send the body home.

facts.statement: Farhad Hossain alias Rony (31), son of Mahamud Sardar of Baguri village, Kayba union, Sharsha, Jashore, a labourer at a construction company in Seremban, Malaysia, died on the spot at about 8 am on Saturday 5 July 2025 when a crane chain snapped while he was working at a building and he was crushed under it.

Farhad Hossain went to Malaysia in January 2023 at a cost of BDT 5 lakh; his father said he borrowed the BDT 5 lakh and had not been able to repay all of it by the time of the son's death in July 2025.

Family members said Bangladeshi workers employed there in Malaysia were trying to bring Farhad's body home, and it might reach the house the following Tuesday (about 8 July 2025); the article mentions no employer, embassy or government role.

The family learned of the death at about 10 am from Abdul Kuddus, a man from the same area who was working beside Farhad. Farhad was the only son and leaves parents, a wife and a five-year-old daughter.

headline_en: Two young men return to Shariatpur destitute
summary_en: Ahsan Ullah and Altaf Hossain (both 30) of Monua village, Bhedarganj, Shariatpur contracted in 2024 with local man Harun Laskar to reach Italy for BDT 16 lakh each. Taken via Sri Lanka, UAE and Egypt to Tripoli, they were twice put on boats that police stopped after 20 minutes ('staged games'), then held in Zawiya, tortured on video call and ransomed. Their families spent BDT 1.30 crore in total (65 lakh each) before they returned on 7 May 2025.

facts.statement: Ahsan Ullah and Altaf Hossain of Monua village, Bhedarganj, Shariatpur each contracted for BDT 16 lakh to go to Italy through Harun Laskar of the neighbouring Banglabazar area.

The two left home on 16 September 2024; they were first taken to Sri Lanka and kept there 24 days, then taken via the United Arab Emirates and Egypt to Tripoli, Libya; on 16 November 2024 they were put on an engine boat from the Tripoli area to go to Italy by sea.

After the boat had run 20 minutes police detained them; the contracted broker got them released from the police, then they were confined at a place in the Zawiya (জাওয়াইয়া) area of Libya and tortured to extract money.

The two contracted again with the same brokers; on 1 January 2025 they were put on a boat from a seaside place called Zuwara (জোয়ারা); again after 20 minutes police detained them at sea; brokers confined them at another place in Zawiya, tortured them, showed the torture to their families on video call and collected ransom, then released them. The victims call these 'staged games' (পাতানো গেম).

Ahsan Ullah first handed the broker BDT 16 lakh; to free him from the 'games' and captivity his family paid the ring a further BDT 49 lakh in four instalments, raised by selling farmland (land had earlier been mortgaged and loans taken to send him).
Altaf Hossain's family spent BDT 65 lakh in five instalments; in total the two families spent BDT 1 crore 30 lakh, including two rounds of ransom, to bring the two back.
After ransom was paid the brokers released the two men, and they returned to Bangladesh on 7 May 2025.

Ahsan Ullah's family filed a complaint against Harun Laskar of Banglabazar, Bhedarganj at Bhedarganj police station; Harun Laskar said he did not know which broker ring harassed or held them hostage and that 'we are not involved'.

Shariatpur Superintendent of Police Nazrul Islam said several rings are involved in illegal human trafficking exploiting local youths' wish to go to Europe, police are working on some cases and have brought several people to justice, and the Bhedarganj incident will also be investigated.
facts.source_in_article: Nazrul Islam, Superintendent of Police, Shariatpur

headline_en: Brawl around BAIRA press conference, followed by rival press conferences
summary_en: On 19 May 2025 a fight broke out at Dhaka Reporters Unity over a press conference by a faction of BAIRA (the recruiting agencies' association) opposing a return of the 'syndicate' in the Malaysia labour market; former joint secretary general Mohammad Fakhrul Islam and others were injured. That faction demanded the ministry reject the syndicate and amend two MoU clauses so Malaysian employers, not the Malaysian government, choose Bangladeshi agencies. The rival group denied there had been a syndicate.

facts.statement: As of 19 May 2025 a BAIRA faction said: 'We want the Malaysian labour market to open quickly for Bangladeshi workers' - indicating the market was not then open - and warned the government against again approving the syndicate system.
facts.source_in_article: written statement read by Mohammad Fakhrul Islam, former joint secretary general, BAIRA

facts.statement: The BAIRA faction led by Fakhrul Islam demanded: the ministry must directly say no to the syndicate; two clauses of the MoU must be cancelled or amended at the two countries' joint technical committee meeting so that the Malaysian employer, rather than the Malaysian government, can choose the Bangladeshi recruiting agency; low-cost sending of workers must be ensured; and the syndicate's ringleaders must be given exemplary punishment.

At its press conference the BAIRA faction presented a summary of irregularities and corruption in the Malaysia labour market under the previous government and offered an alternative proposal to send workers at low cost without a syndicate.

Fakhrul Islam alleged the attackers were linked to the syndicate of the previous government's era and came on the instructions of 'syndicate-holders' Ruhul Amin Swapon and Kazi Rafiq; he named BAIRA members Atik, Fatema, Nazim Uddin Bhuiyan and Hasan Mahmud among the attackers.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Fakhrul Islam, former joint secretary general, BAIRA

facts.statement: The fight took place at about 11:30 am in the office room of Dhaka Reporters Unity, Segunbagicha, and again about noon outside; Fakhrul Islam said 70-80 people tried to enter the Sagar-Runi hall and attacked him, breaking his nose and injuring his eye; Nazrul Islam Monir, proprietor of Al Habib Trading, said he was dragged down the stairs.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Fakhrul Islam; Nazrul Islam Monir

facts.statement: At a counter press conference Atikur Rahman Atik, proprietor of Al Aqaba Associate, said the Fakhrul group were Awami League collaborators who wanted to shut the Malaysia labour market by raising the syndicate issue; Mezbah Uddin Sayeed, director of Instance International Limited (ইনসট্যানস ইন্টারন্যাশনাল), said 'there was no syndicate', it was hype, and they want people to be able to go to Malaysia through talks between the two governments.

headline_en: Mediterranean boat sinking: Madaripur youth returns from Libya as a corpse
summary_en: Rifat Talukdar (25) of Shibchar, Madaripur left in October 2024 via Dubai for Libya and on 18 December 2024 set out for Italy; the boat sank after an engine explosion and he died two days later in a Libyan hospital. The family applied to the Foreign Ministry on 5 January 2025; the body was traced in a Libyan hospital morgue on 26 March 2025 and brought home at government expense, reaching the village on 10 May 2025.

facts.statement: Rifat Talukdar (25) of Talukdarkandi village, Ditiyakhanda union, Shibchar, Madaripur left Bangladesh in October 2024 through a local broker, went via Dubai to Libya, waited there two months, and on 18 December 2024 set out across the Mediterranean for Italy.
Rifat's boat sank after an engine explosion; he was seriously injured, rescued by the Libyan coast guard and admitted to a hospital in Libya, where he died two days later.

After losing contact, Rifat's family applied to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 5 January 2025 to trace him; on 26 March 2025 his body was found in the morgue of a hospital in Libya; the body was then brought from Libya to Bangladesh officially and reached the village home on Saturday 10 May 2025, about five months after death.

Shibchar UNO Parvin Khanam said the body of the would-be migrant was delivered from Libya to his family with government funding, and the administration will provide all kinds of help if the family asks.

headline_en: Tortured after BDT 46 lakh was taken on promise of Italy; finally dies
summary_en: Sajib Sardar (29) of Shibchar, Madaripur died in a Libyan hospital on 19 March 2025 after months of torture in captivity. His family contracted with broker Borhan Bepari for BDT 16 lakh to reach Italy; he was taken via Dubai to Libya in November 2024, sold twice to 'mafia', and the family paid BDT 30 lakh ransom in two instalments after receiving torture videos - BDT 46 lakh in all. The broker says his contract was only up to Libya; no complaint had yet been filed with police.

facts.statement: The family of Sajib Sardar (29) of Bagmara, Nilokhi union, Shibchar, Madaripur contracted with a local broker for BDT 16 lakh to deliver him to Italy; he left home in November 2024.
The broker took Sajib from Dhaka via Dubai to Libya; on arrival in Libya he was passed to another broker ring, and brokers in Libya detained him in a holding cell (bandishala).

The local broker told the family Sajib had been taken hostage by 'mafia' and demanded BDT 30 lakh ransom; videos of him being tortured were sent to the family's phone with threats to kill him if the money was not paid.
Sajib's family sold land and borrowed to pay BDT 30 lakh ransom in two instalments; with the BDT 16 lakh contract money his sister says the broker took BDT 46 lakh in instalments.
facts.source_in_article: Chanmia Sardar, father; Shamima Akter, sister

facts.statement: Locals say broker Borhan Bepari first took Sajib to Libya on a BDT 16 lakh contract for Italy, then he was sold to mafia on the pretext of a 'game' (the boat crossing of the Mediterranean) direct to Italy; Sajib was sold twice and beaten to extract BDT 30 lakh in two rounds.

Sajib was held about four months, chained with iron chains, beaten and not fed properly; when he became seriously ill he was released into the care of another broker in Libya who admitted him to a hospital in Libya, where he died on the night of Wednesday 19 March 2025.
facts.source_in_article: Chanmia Sardar, father; Julekha Begum, mother; local sources

facts.statement: Broker Borhan Bepari of Shirkhara area, Madaripur Sadar, said by phone: 'My contract was to take him as far as Libya. I don't know what happened after that. There is no use blaming me.'

Shibchar police OC Md. Ratan Sheikh said the family had not yet filed any complaint accusing a broker, and legal action would be taken if they complain; UNO Parvin Khanam said help would be given if the family asks and necessary steps would be taken to bring the body.

headline_en: Did Pratik Group chairman stage a BDT 730 crore 'remittance drama' to whiten black money?
summary_en: After the NBR chairman said on 17 March 2025 that a businessman had brought in BDT 730 crore as tax-free remittance with cash incentive, Prothom Alo found it was BDT 721 crore from China over nine years, brought by Pratik Group chairman Syed Mohammad Faruqui Hasan and shown as wage-earner income. Tax officials suspect laundered or commission money; his bank accounts have been frozen and NBR's tax intelligence unit is investigating. The article notes remittance is tax-free and earns a government cash incentive.

facts.statement: In Bangladesh there is no tax on remittance (expatriate income) brought into the country, and money brought as remittance also receives a government cash incentive; such money is shown as wage-earner income in the tax file and few questions are asked.

NBR chairman Abdur Rahman Khan said on Monday 17 March 2025 that a businessman had brought in BDT 730 crore as remittance using the tax exemption and cash incentive; Prothom Alo found the amount was BDT 721 crore from China, by a taxpayer of Dhaka Tax Zone-5, Pratik Group chairman Syed Mohammad Faruqui Hasan. His and his firms' bank accounts have been frozen and NBR's tax intelligence unit is investigating.
facts.source_in_article: NBR chairman; reporter's inquiry; Tax Zone-5

facts.statement: The money came over nine years as 'remittance' from three Chinese firms - Norinco International Corporation, China Shipbuilding and Offshore International Company: BDT 269 crore in FY2021-22, BDT 77 crore and BDT 81 crore in the two preceding years, and about BDT 300 crore in four earlier years - all shown as remittance in tax files, allegedly with tax officials' collusion.

Tax officials explain that money laundered abroad through trade or hundi, or commissions paid abroad by big companies, can be brought back as 'remittance', becoming legal in the tax file without tax and even earning the cash incentive.

headline_en: Women workers going abroad have been falling for two years
summary_en: BMET data show women's overseas employment fell from 105,466 in 2022 to 76,108 in 2023 and 61,158 in 2024. Most go to the Middle East as domestic workers (66% to Saudi Arabia in 2024); returnees describe unpaid or low wages, lack of food, beatings and untreated injury. BAIRA says training was lengthened from one to two months and Saudi employers are now hiring from African countries.

facts.statement: BMET data: 105,466 women workers went abroad from Bangladesh in 2022, 76,108 in 2023 and 61,158 in 2024 - a fall of 28% from 2022 to 2023 and 20% from 2023 to 2024.

In the three years to 2024 more than 34 lakh workers went abroad in total, of whom fewer than 2.5 lakh were women. From 2015 to 2019 more than one lakh women went abroad every year; the number fell in 2020 due to Covid, rose for two years, then fell for two years.

BMET data: in 2024 women workers went to 56 countries; fewer than 10 went to each of 30 countries, only one each to 16 countries; more than 1,000 each went to five countries - Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Qatar, UAE and the United Kingdom. Saudi Arabia took 66% of all women workers in 2024, more than 40,000.
The pre-departure training for women workers going abroad has been increased from one month to two months, lengthening the process time for sending women workers.
facts.source_in_article: Ali Haider Chowdhury, secretary general, BAIRA

facts.statement: BAIRA's secretary general said Saudi employers are no longer placing demand for Bangladeshi women domestic workers as before and are now taking workers from various African countries; negative publicity about sending domestic workers has also reduced interest in going.
facts.source_in_article: Ali Haider Chowdhury, secretary general, BAIRA

facts.statement: Firoza of Manikganj returned ill in October 2024 after two years in Saudi Arabia: in the first year pay was low but regular; in the second year pay was raised but not paid for 11 straight months, and all of it was paid together when she left; food was a problem and she was beaten. She says women should not go to Saudi Arabia for housework.

Shahida Begum (40) of Faridpur returned in October 2024 after two years three months in one Saudi household: food was irregular, pay was low, the kafeel's (employer's) son sometimes beat her, and she got no treatment after spraining her leg on the stairs. Although the employer was supposed to give the return ticket, 700 riyals (BDT 17,500) was deducted from her pay.

Officials of BRAC, OKUP (Ovibashi Karmi Unnayan Program) and Nari Sramik Kendra say returning women's complaints include being taken on false promises, being made to work in several houses, 14 to 16 hours of work, low and irregular pay, irregular food, and for some physical and mental torture; suicides have occurred, and some who fled the kafeel's house were detained by police and returned.
facts.source_in_article: officials of BRAC, OKUP and Nari Sramik Kendra

facts.statement: BRAC, OKUP (a grassroots migrants' organisation) and Nari Sramik Kendra provide various services to workers who return from abroad.

OKUP chairperson Shakirul Islam said hardly any work opportunities have been created for women in sectors other than domestic work, and awareness that women regularly return abused from housework has made women unwilling to go on false promises.

headline_en: Human trafficking case in Sylhet filed on false allegations, press conference claims
summary_en: A case under the human trafficking law was recorded at Sylhet Kotwali police station on 4 December 2024 against 12 people for allegedly trafficking a Sunamganj youth, Ali Hossain (28), to Libya on a promise of Spain; his father says he paid about BDT 25 lakh and has had no contact for three and a half months. On 11 December a nephew of the main accused told a press conference the case is false and that the complainant and his son themselves hold people hostage in Libya.

facts.statement: Abdul Haque (55) of Sridharpasha village, Jagannathpur, Sunamganj filed a complaint petition on 27 November 2024 at the Sylhet Human Trafficking Crimes Suppression Tribunal alleging his son Ali Hossain (28) was trafficked to Libya on an assurance of being sent to Spain; on 4 December 2024 it was recorded as a case under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act at Sylhet Kotwali Model police station against 12 accused.

The main accused is Faysal Mia (45) of Akhalia area, Sylhet city; other accused named are his brother Mokbul Mia; Hasan Nur and Saiful Islam of Sridharpasha, Enam of Asampur, Shahin of Parargaon and Jilu Mia of Sridharpasha (all Jagannathpur); Nazrul Islam of Topoban area, Sylhet city; and Saleh of Doulatpur village, Derai.

Complainant Abdul Haque said the accused (Faysal and others) are holding his son hostage in Libya, that he has paid about BDT 25 lakh in all on promises of release, that they did not send the son back, and that he has had no contact with his son for three and a half months and does not know where he is.

At a press conference at Sylhet District Press Club on Wednesday 11 December 2024, Iqbal Hossain, nephew of main accused Faysal Mia, claimed the case is false; he alleged that Abdul Haque's son Ali Hossain has lived in Libya since 2015 and that father and son take well-off local boys to Libya in the name of sending them to European countries, hold them hostage and extract lakhs of taka, that two people have died in Libya from their torture, and that Abdul Haque and his wife were arrested over it. He demanded a fair investigation.

headline_en: Bangladeshis wishing to return from Lebanon must register
summary_en: On 9 October 2024 the Foreign Ministry said the Bangladesh Embassy in Beirut has asked Bangladeshis who want to return home from war-hit Lebanon to register their names; about 1,000 migrant workers initially want to return. The government asked IOM to arrange chartered flights, but Beirut airport is not currently safe for flights, so alternative places outside the war zone are being sought.

facts.statement: The Bangladesh Embassy in Beirut has asked Bangladeshis who wish to return home from Lebanon to register their names, according to a Ministry of Foreign Affairs press release of Wednesday 9 October 2024.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Foreign Affairs press release

facts.statement: According to initial information, about 1,000 Bangladeshi migrant workers want to return home from Lebanon.

The government says it is committed to bringing back all citizens who wish to return from Lebanon; the Foreign Ministry and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment are making coordinated efforts, and a recent inter-ministerial meeting prepared a framework for bringing back Bangladeshis from Lebanon. Steps are also being taken for the safety of those who wish to stay.

Foreign Adviser Md. Touhid Hossain said on Tuesday 8 October 2024 that the government has asked the International Organization for Migration (IOM) to arrange chartered flights to evacuate stranded Bangladeshis from Lebanon; the challenge is that Beirut airport is currently not safe for flights, and Bangladesh has advised finding alternative places outside the war zone for the evacuation.
Foreign Secretary Md. Jashim Uddin instructed the ambassador to ensure Bangladeshi citizens are brought home safely; the embassy is working closely with stakeholders on security and timely transport.

Israel began air strikes on Lebanon on 17 September 2024 and a ground attack through the southern border on 30 September 2024; attacks continued in Beirut and other regions and many countries were evacuating their nationals.

headline_en: Al-Amin receives US 'TIP Hero' award for work against human trafficking
summary_en: On 24 June 2024 in Washington, US Secretary of State Antony Blinken gave the 'TIP Hero' award to Al-Amin (Noyon), manager of BRAC's Migration Welfare Centre, who was himself trafficked when he went to work in Malaysia in 2007. He assists returnees and trafficking victims at Dhaka airport and is said to have helped at least 34,000 people. A case filed against him in December 2023 was condemned by migrant organisations; he is on bail.

facts.statement: BRAC runs a Migration Welfare Centre whose manager, Al-Amin (Noyon), assists returnees from abroad and trafficking victims; he goes to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka whenever expatriates are in trouble, and when a mentally ill or addressless worker is found at the airport the Probashi Kalyan Desk or Airport Armed Police phone him.
As manager of BRAC's Migration Welfare Centre, Al-Amin is said to have assisted at least 34,000 returnees and trafficking victims; he began working in the BRAC Migration Programme in 2017.

Al-Amin went to Malaysia for work in 2007, became a victim of human trafficking and returned to Bangladesh the same year; after return he began a fight for his own rights and compensation and joined the movement for trafficking victims' and migrants' rights.
During the Covid pandemic Al-Amin worked on food, medical care and delivering returning expatriates to their families.
'Anirban Survivor Voice' (অনির্বাণ সারভাইভার ভয়েস) is described as the largest network of human trafficking survivors in Bangladesh; Al-Amin is its president.
A case was filed against Al-Amin in December 2023; all organisations working on migration condemned his arrest, calling the case false and harassing; he is currently on bail in the case.

The US State Department has honoured anti-trafficking individuals every year since 2004; in 2024 nine people were recognised as TIP Heroes (Bangladesh, Kenya, Mali, Philippines, Serbia, Spain, Suriname, Bolivia and Iraq), Al-Amin being the only one from South Asia; the award was handed over at the release of the annual Trafficking in Persons report in Washington.

headline_en: Remittances sent to siblings and in-laws also to be taxed
summary_en: Under the FY2024-25 budget proposal (reported 16 June 2024), cash, gifts and remittances received from anyone other than a spouse, children or parents would be treated as the recipient's income and taxed at up to 30%. An NBR official said tax can be avoided only if the sender declares the money as his own and the recipient shows it as a liability; NBR had given no formal clarification. PRI's Ahsan H Mansur criticised the move and suggested joint accounts.

facts.statement: According to the budget proposal, cash, gifts and remittances received from anyone other than husband/wife, son/daughter or mother/father would be taxable: remittance arriving in the bank account of a sibling, in-law, other relative or friend would be treated as that recipient's capital income (a gift), taxable at a rate of up to 30%, provided the recipient is within the tax net.
Under the proposal a gift recipient must show the gift in the annual income tax return and the giver must also report it in his or her return.

An NBR official explained the way to avoid the tax: the person who sent the remittance must show it as his own money (declare that it was given as a loan or kept in the recipient's custody), and the recipient must show it as a liability in the return; only then is it free of tax.

There is no tax on remittance in Bangladesh; so how the new budget would tax remittance money was unclear and NBR had given no formal explanation as of 16 June 2024; NBR officials said it might be clarified when the income tax circular (paripatra) is issued.

PRI executive director Ahsan H Mansur advised that a migrant who regularly sends money to siblings, friends or in-laws can open a joint bank account with them; alternatively, if the wife has no bank account the worker can send the money to a brother or brother-in-law who passes it on to the wife, but a written document is needed. He said the NBR proposal is inconsistent with the government's overall remittance policy.
facts.source_in_article: Ahsan H Mansur, executive director, Policy Research Institute

facts.statement: NBR officials said opening a bank account is now very easy, and with an account the parent, spouse or child to whom the money is sent would receive it directly. The article notes that in villages many elderly parents have no bank account, children are minors or wives do not open accounts, so migrants often rely on siblings', friends' or relatives' accounts, through legal channels.
By Bangladesh Bank's count USD 2,000 to 2,500 crore in remittances come through legal channels each year, besides large amounts through hundi or illegal channels.

By the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment's count, 1,125,833 workers went abroad with jobs in FY2022-23, the largest number, about 4.5 lakh, to Saudi Arabia; the number of Bangladeshis abroad is now about 1 crore.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment

key_quote_bn: কর আরোপ না করার উপায় হলো, যিনি রেমিট্যান্স পাঠিয়েছেন, তাঁকে তা নিজের অর্থ হিসেবে দেখাতে হবে। যিনি পেয়েছেন, তাঁকে রিটার্নে তা দায় হিসেবে দেখাতে হবে।

headline_en: Oman will regularise 96,000 Bangladeshi workers: state minister
summary_en: After visiting Dubai, Qatar and Oman, State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury said (ministry release, 11 June 2024) that Oman has assured it will reopen its labour market to new Bangladeshi workers and regularise 96,000 Bangladeshis living there illegally, waiving a fine of BDT 12,000 per worker per month at Bangladesh's request. Oman wants skilled workers in 12 sectors; unskilled workers can go after skilled sending begins.

facts.statement: Oman has given an assurance that it will open its labour market to take new workers from Bangladesh, the State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare said after visiting Oman from 24 to 31 May 2024.
facts.source_in_article: Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury, State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment

facts.statement: The state minister said 96,000 Bangladeshi workers are living illegally in Oman and the Omani government has assured it will regularise them; each worker was supposed to pay a fine of BDT 12,000 per month for this, but it has been waived at Bangladesh's request.
Oman wants to take skilled workers in 12 sectors; once sending of skilled workers begins, unskilled workers will also be able to go, according to the ministry's press release of 11 June 2024.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment press release

facts.statement: The state minister met Qatar's labour minister Ali bin Samikh Al Marri and discussed various worker issues; sending more workers to the United Arab Emirates was discussed during his Dubai visit.

key_quote_bn: এর জন্য প্রত্যেক কর্মীকে মাসে ১২ হাজার টাকা জরিমানা দেওয়ার কথা থাকলেও বাংলাদেশের অনুরোধে এটি মওকুফ করা হয়েছে।

headline_en: Why they were left out is being investigated: Prime Minister in Parliament
summary_en: In Parliament on 5 June 2024, PM Sheikh Hasina said the government is investigating why many workers could not travel to Malaysia despite special flights, and action will be taken against anyone responsible. Opposition chief whip Mujibul Haque said Malaysia takes workers from 14 countries and only for Bangladesh must workers go through a few selected agencies. Hasina urged people not to sell land and to take Probashi Kallyan Bank loans instead. The rest of the article covers unrelated parliamentary answers.

facts.statement: PM Sheikh Hasina told Parliament on 5 June 2024 that the government had started special flights to send workers to Malaysia and sent people by special flights linked with other flights, but many were still left out; the reason is being investigated and action will be taken if anyone is responsible.
facts.source_in_article: Sheikh Hasina, Prime Minister, in Parliament

facts.statement: Opposition chief whip Mujibul Haque told Parliament that Malaysia takes workers from 14 countries; in 13 of them all licensed legal agencies can send workers, and only in Bangladesh's case must workers be sent through a few specific agencies arranged by some people of Malaysia and Bangladesh together (a 'ring'). He asked why all legal Bangladeshi agencies cannot send workers.
facts.source_in_article: Mujibul Haque, opposition chief whip, in Parliament

facts.statement: Sheikh Hasina said that whenever the government negotiates and fixes how many will go, a class of manpower businessmen in Bangladesh, linked with some people in Malaysia, rush to send people and create an abnormal situation; those who go find their work, job and wages are not as promised and fall into danger there - and this happens in many places, not only Malaysia.

Sheikh Hasina said people need not sell land and houses and spend lakhs of taka to go abroad; if needed they can take a loan from Probashi Kallyan Bank, which gives loans without collateral where necessary, provided the person specifies that he is going and that his job is definite.

The Prime Minister said some people want to go abroad through brokers and get into trouble, while those who go following the rules do not face problems; some sell everything in the race to go first and end up destitute or in danger abroad.

key_quote_bn: যদি দরকার হয়, প্রবাসী কল্যাণ ব্যাংক থেকে ঋণ নিতে পারেন। প্রয়োজনবোধে বিনা জামানতে ঋণ দেওয়া হয়।

headline_en: 'The brokers gave dates two or three times and never kept their word'
summary_en: Meraj Mia of Debgram, Akhaura, Brahmanbaria sold land and paid a broker BDT 6.5 lakh a year earlier to send his son Tanvir Mia alias Sohel (22) to Malaysia for a supershop job. Flight dates on 19 January 2024 and again on Friday 31 May 2024 were cancelled at the last moment. Returning home by train that day, Tanvir fell from the train door into the Meghna at Bhairab and is presumed drowned; the family blames broker Alamgir Hossain.

facts.statement: Meraj Mia of Debgram, Akhaura, Brahmanbaria sold land and paid BDT 6.5 lakh about a year before June 2024 to broker Alamgir Hossain of Noyadil village, Akhaura and his Malaysia-based brother to send his son Tanvir Mia alias Sohel (22) to Malaysia; the broker had promised a supershop job, and the son's passport was made on an urgent basis.
facts.source_in_article: Meraj Mia's family; Imran Hossain, maternal uncle

facts.statement: The broker first gave a flight date of 19 January 2024 and said at the last moment the flight was cancelled; after the broker sent 30 people to Malaysia a few days before, the family trusted him and went to Dhaka on Thursday 30 May 2024 for a flight due on Friday 31 May morning or noon, which was again cancelled. The uncle says the brokers gave dates two or three times and did not keep their word.
facts.source_in_article: Imran Hossain, maternal uncle of Tanvir

facts.statement: On Friday 31 May 2024, returning home on the intercity 'Upakul Express' train after the cancelled Malaysia flight, Tanvir fell from the train door into the Meghna river at the Bhairab rail bridge, Kishoreganj and went missing; Bhairab river police and Fire Service divers searched, the rescue was called off at noon on 2 June 2024, and rescuers presume he drowned.

Broker Alamgir Hossain of Noyadil village, Akhaura could not be reached despite several calls to his mobile; Tanvir's uncle called him a 'killer' whose shifting words cost his nephew's life. Many others were supposed to travel along with Tanvir.
Tanvir's father sold 130 decimals of land to send his son abroad and for his own business.

headline_en: More than 1.5 crore workers went abroad in 48 years: state minister in Parliament
summary_en: State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury told Parliament on 8 May 2024 that 16,312,324 workers went abroad for employment from 1976 to March 2024, to 176 countries; the ministry has no data on Bangladeshis living abroad illegally without passports. He also gave figures for FY2023-24 and for low- or no-cost government-channel migration. The article ends with unrelated answers from the labour and food ministers.

facts.statement: From 1976 to March 2024 (48 years), 16,312,324 (1 crore 63 lakh 12 thousand 324) workers went abroad from Bangladesh for overseas employment.
facts.source_in_article: Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury, State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare, in Parliament

facts.statement: The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment has no information on how many Bangladeshis without passports are living illegally in various countries.
The state minister said the number of workers sent abroad in FY2023-24 was 1,126,060 (11 lakh 26 thousand 60), and that the overseas labour market had recovered after Covid.
Workers have been sent from Bangladesh to 176 countries so far.
From FY2009-10 to FY2022-23, 127,557 workers went abroad through government channels at low or no cost.

key_quote_bn: ২০০৯-১০ থেকে ২০২২-২৩ অর্থবছর পর্যন্ত সরকারিভাবে স্বল্প বা বিনা খরচে ১ লাখ ২৭ হাজার ৫৫৭ জন কর্মী বিদেশে গেছেন।

headline_en: Video of youth being tortured in Libya sent, BDT 10 lakh ransom demanded
summary_en: Rubel Hossain of Gabtali, Bogura went to Libya in mid-January 2024 through broker Mizanur Rahman alias Dholu of Temaria village, Akkelpur, Joypurhat after paying BDT 4 lakh. Moved elsewhere in Libya on a promise of better work, he was confined and beaten; a video was sent by WhatsApp on 27 March 2024 and a Bangladeshi caller demanded BDT 10 lakh ransom. The broker, who lives in Libya and recruits through his father and brother, is unreachable and his family has fled.

facts.statement: Rubel Hossain of Ameshwarpur Nishipara village, Gabtali, Bogura sold his land and gave BDT 4 lakh to relatives of broker Mizanur Rahman alias Dholu; he went to Libya in the second week of January 2024.

Broker Mizanur kept Rubel idle in Libya; about 10 days before 31 March 2024 Rubel was taken to another place in Libya on the promise of good work, confined there and beaten. On 27 March 2024 a video was sent to a relative's WhatsApp showing him in a room with hands and feet tied together and cloth stuffed in his mouth being beaten with a stick.
facts.source_in_article: Aktarun, elder sister of Rubel's wife

facts.statement: An unknown-voiced Bangladeshi phoned from Libya demanding BDT 10 lakh ransom for Rubel and threatening to kill him otherwise; on Saturday 30 March 2024 Rubel's wife was phoned again with the BDT 10 lakh demand.
facts.source_in_article: Aktarun, elder sister of Rubel's wife

facts.statement: Villagers say broker Mizanur Rahman alias Dholu of Temaria village, Akkelpur, Joypurhat spent 10 years in Saudi Arabia, returned three years ago, ran fish and poultry farms, went to Libya a year and a half ago and then began taking people to Libya; his father Abdur Rahman and younger brother Shahin went around recruiting people to send to Libya.

After a video of four youths from Anwara, Chattogram being tortured in Libya spread, people from various places began coming to Mizanur's house; on Tuesday 26 March 2024, 20-25 strangers on eight motorcycles took away his son Romim, who was recovered by relatives that night; on Friday 29 March his parents and brother locked the house and left for an unknown place. Mizanur cannot be reached by phone.
facts.source_in_article: villagers; Aktarun; UP member Fazilatun Nesa

facts.statement: Gopinathpur UP reserved woman member Fazilatun Nesa said Mizanur took many people to Libya and she now hears he is confining people in Libya and demanding ransom; Hafizar Rahman of Temaria said Mizanur took his son to Libya two weeks earlier and the family cannot now trace him.
facts.source_in_article: Fazilatun Nesa, UP member; Hafizar Rahman
